Signs of the World

Gas station

History

The first modern filling station is thought to have opened in 1905 in St. Louis, Missouri. The filling station symbol appears in the 1949 Geneva Protocol on Road Signs and Signals, with an old-style globe-topped pump set on blue. The 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals recommends a modern version of the symbol.

Adoption

The gas station symbol appears anywhere gasoline provides a means of travel, with minor variations across countries.
